Where childhood memories are made and futures are nurtured
Kitebrook Preparatory School is a day and boarding school set within the beautiful Cotswold countryside and epitomises what a great country school should be.
Nestled in the heart of the beautiful Cotswold countryside, Kitebrook Preparatory School is a thriving day and boarding school that perfectly captures the spirit of a traditional English country prep. Our idyllic rural setting provides the perfect backdrop for a truly enriching childhood, one filled with learning, laughter and the freedom to explore.
At Kitebrook, we provide an outstanding all-round education for boys and girls aged 3 to 13, enabling every pupil to develop at their own pace within a happy, nurturing and inspiring environment. We believe that children learn best when they feel confident, valued and supported and our dedicated team of teachers ensures that every child is encouraged to discover their individual strengths and passions.
Our pupils enjoy the freedom of childhood in the best sense of the word. With acres of beauitful grounds to roam, they build dens, climb trees and make lasting memories with friends. Whether in the classroom, on the sports field or simply exploring nature, Kitebrook children are encouraged to be curious, adventurous and kind.
We combine high academic standards with a stimulating curriculum, supported by specialist teaching across a wide range of subjects. From music and art to science, sport and drama, every opportunity is provided for pupils to flourish both intellectually and creatively. Our approach ensures that children leave Kitebrook as confident, balanced and compassionate young people, fully prepared for the next step of their educational journey.
Above all, we believe that a child’s school days should be some of the happiest of their lives. At Kitebrook, we celebrate the joy of learning, the beauty of the countryside, and the boundless potential of every child.

Partnerships
We believe that strong community partnerships enrich our pupils’ educational experience and foster a deep sense of service and connection. By working closely with local organisations and initiatives, we create meaningful opportunities for engagement that extend beyond the classroom.
Connecting with Cotswold Friends
Our partnership with Cotswold Friends has brought rewarding connections, as we regularly host events that build lasting relationships. Through these interactions, our pupils develop empathy, understanding, and a greater appreciation for their wider community.
North Cotswold Rota Kids: Young Leaders in Action
Our newly formed North Cotswold Rota Kids, made up of ten dedicated pupils, exemplifies our commitment to service. From charitable events and fundraising initiatives to crocus planting projects, these young leaders actively contribute to the well-being of the local community.
Bringing the Community Together
Community Days are a cornerstone of life at Kitebrook, uniting our school with the wider community. Our hugely popular Dog Show has been a highlight, and we are excited to introduce a 5K and/or Triathlon. These events are designed to bring families, friends, and neighbours together in a spirit of fun and shared achievement.
Celebrating Together
Throughout the year, we host events that strengthen our school community, including World Book Day,Medieval Days, Sports Days, and Prayers that incorporate the parent body – an integral part of life at Kitebrook. These moments of togetherness create shared experiences and a sense of belonging for all.
Local Residents Partnership
Our Local Residents Partnership ensures that those around us feel valued and included. Through regular meetings and open communication, we reinforce our dedication to being a school that truly belongs to its community.

Co-Curricular Clubs
Kitebrook offers a wide variety of clubs, with sign-ups available to parents before the start of each term.
Our club programme is designed to be diverse, reflecting the many talents, skills, and interests of our pupils. External providers lead our sports clubs, which include:
Beyond sports, we provide clubs that spark imagination, develop critical thinking, and encourage outdoor exploration in our beautiful school grounds and Forest School area. For those interested in the performing arts, we offer Choral Club, Orchestra, Woodwind, Drama, and Young Voices Clubs. From Den Building, Chess, STEM, and Art to Coding and Gardening, there’s something for every child to enjoy.
Pathways
Our pathways, offered by teacher invitation, run before or after school and help pupils deepen their interests in specific subjects. These may be for those preparing scholarship portfolios for senior schools or for those wanting to refine their skills in a particular craft. We offer Art, Drama, Sport, and Music Pathways, along with swimming, cross-country, and other sporting activities.

Seniors
At Kitebrook, the majority of our pupils choose to stay with us throughout their Senior years, from Year 6 to Year 8. We offer a comprehensive curriculum that follows the Common Entrance Syllabus, ensuring that our pupils are well-prepared for the next stages of their education.
Curriculum and Specialist Teaching
Our Senior curriculum is enriched by specialist subject teaching, allowing pupils to delve deeper into their areas of interest and gain a robust understanding of core subjects. The key subjects offered include:
In Senior, pupils benefit from a tutor system rather than a traditional class teacher structure. This arrangement encourages open communication between pupils and their tutors, who work to establish a strong rapport and sense of trust with each tutee. This supportive environment allows pupils to discuss their academic progress and personal development freely.

Arts
The Arts at Kitebrook thrive through a dynamic and diverse offering in Performing Arts, Music, and Art.
Performing Arts
This is manifest in the enhanced scope of opportunities both within Performing Arts lessons and in the growing range of extra-curricular options available to all pupils within the school. This includes: Drama, Dance and Stagecraft, the Drama Pathway for potential scholars as well as the option of taking solo or group LAMDA lessons leading to additional external examinations. In addition, our new Performing Arts curriculum ensures that all pupils are exposed to content above and beyond the expectation for their age group in readiness for Drama studies at the pupils’ chosen senior school. This encompasses the preparatory study of specific GCSE techniques, theoretical topics and the exploration of leading theatre practitioners, methods and styles.
Music
The Music Department delivers a busy extra-curricular programme including the school orchestra and two choirs. There are peripatetic lessons on all orchestral instruments as well as singing, piano and classical guitar. In addition there are a range of highlights during the musical year including the Harvest Festival, Carol Service, Remembrance Service and music’s special place at the end of year Prize Giving ceremony. Furthermore, pupils are encouraged to participate in the wide ranging opportunities to attend concerts and other musical events outside school. Pupils from Kitebrook regularly achieve Music scholarships and awards to senior schools as well as taking part in music and musical theatre opportunities beyond the regular school curriculum.
Art
Art at Kitebrook continues to provide an exciting opportunity for pupils to explore a fascinating range of artistic challenges in our purpose built studio and surrounded by a perfect aesthetic setting. We aim to enrich the work of every child through the use of our bespoke and individual sketchbook scheme. Participation in our after school art extension club provides a further opportunity for all enthusiastic, gifted and talented artists. Within the Art curriculum pupils study a wide range of interesting contemporary and historical artists and we encourage pupils to attend relevant exhibitions, some of which are organised as part of the school curriculum. From the Lewis Chessmen, the Bayeux Tapestry, Paul Nash and the war artists through to contemporary artists such as Althea McNish and Kehinde Wiley —there is always something new and stimulating to discover in Art.

Bursaries
As a Prep Schools Trust School our bursaries are administered by the Trust.
Their Bursary Policy has been authorised by the Trustees and forms part of the Trust’s Public Benefit Strategy. The aim of the policy is to ensure that prospective and current parents/guardians are aware of the bursary provision and the process by which they can apply. The Trustees are committed to assisting access to the Trust’s schools by offering means-tested financial support with the payment of school fees. Such support is known as a Bursary and these may be awarded in the form of a discount of up to 100% of the day tuition fees, depending on the financial circumstances of applicants.
For further information and for the bursary policy, please visit the Prep Schools Trust website here.

PECK
PECK, our Parent Events Committee of Kitebrook, plays a key role in fostering communication and collaboration between the school and parents.
PECK organises fun activities for pupils, including a Father Christmas visit, Easter Egg Hunt, and Ice Cream van visit. They also support school-run events such as parent welcome drinks, the summer ball, and the summer fair.
Additionally, each year group has two parent representatives who act as points of contact and help organise class-specific or parent-focused events, like coffee mornings.
PECK welcomes any involvement from parents, whether through volunteering or joining the committee. Please contact Mrs Eddie Peters for further information.

Sport
Sport plays a key part of life at our school. Children participate in a variety of team sports as part of the curriculum, including rugby, hockey, netball, football, rounders, cricket, lacrosse, fitness and cross country, athletics, swimming, tennis, and golf.
Sporting fixtures from Year 4 upwards take place on Tuesday and Wednesday afternoons, where every pupil is given the opportunity to represent the school. These are against other preparatory schools and are aimed at encouraging self-confidence, self-esteem, teamwork, and sportsmanship. A mixture of both home, away and inter-house fixtures are all part of our extremely busy sporting calendar, as well as residential sporting trips.
Our talented, committed and professional sports staff also offer sports clinics, pathways and additional 1 to 1 sessions aimed at guiding our gifted and talented pupils to achieve both district and county honours, as well as scholarships at their secondary schools.
Our main goal at Kitebrook is to encourage all pupils to love sport and to take away the necessary skills to enjoy sport and exercise into adult life. We strive to develop the sporting skills necessary to appreciate the value of ‘sport for life’.

Pastoral Care
We understand that for young people to thrive both inside and outside the classroom, they need to feel valued and fully supported by a strong pastoral care system.
This remains a key priority for us, overseen by our Assistant Head (Pastoral Care), Mrs Paget. From Pre-School through to Year 8, we empower each child to care for themselves and others, fostering a sense of respect and kindness.
We place a strong emphasis on mental health, equipping our pupils with the resilience to handle challenges and the courage to seek help when needed. Our small class sizes allow us to offer personalised care through a tailored and nurturing programme. Teachers, boarding staff, office staff, and Heads of Section are always available to support pupils. We also provide access to an in-house School Counsellor and a therapy dog for those who need an additional listening ear or a comforting presence.
Pastoral care works best when school and parents collaborate. We maintain regular communication with families and offer training courses for both staff and parents, ensuring a united approach to supporting our children.
Kitebrook is proud to be a mobile phone free site for pupils, parents, and staff, helping to promote focus, mindfulness, and meaningful face-to-face interactions.
Kitebrook is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of all pupils.

Our History
In 1959, Anne McDermott founded Kitebrook with the vision of creating a school that offered not only academic excellence but also a close-knit, family-like environment where freedom of thought, individual growth, and mutual respect and trust would flourish.
Today, we proudly uphold the rich legacy she began, continuing to provide a vibrant, dynamic education rooted in the values she cherished. The love of children, dignity, and passion for learning that Mrs McDermott instilled still resonates through our school corridors and grounds. This is especially evident in the daily life of our pupils, who are immersed in an almost Enid Blyton-like existence, with acres of countryside to explore and trees to climb.
Break times are filled with adventure, as children scale the towering trees that line the grounds, some with ropes, ladders, and swings to enhance their play. Friends gather at the treetops, enjoying the freedom to explore and create memories, with the occasional teacher lending a helping hand when needed.
Mrs McDermott created something truly unique and special, and we are honoured to carry forward the greatness she exemplified at Kitebrook, blending the joy of nature with a love for learning.

Outdoor Education
Kitebrook is very proud to include Outdoor Education as part of its rich curriculum.
At least once a week, all year groups will take part in some form of outdoor learning. We use our forest school, the walled garden, and all our stunning grounds, to help inspire our children to love the outdoors and develop many different practical skills.
Our Outdoor Education falls into three categories:
The first is learning about the value of the outdoors; be it nature, farming, animals or the developing seasons.
The second is taking the curriculum outdoors; Mathematics, English, Drama or History, the children will get a chance to work and explore the practical nature of their subjects out in the open air. What could be a more inspiring way to write a powerful story in your very own secret garden?
The final area is linked to the Growth Mindset. We are very proud of our children’s ability to focus, persevere and collaborate with all. Many practical activities will help them to enhance all their personal and social skills, whilst having plenty of fun along the way.

Oral English
Kitebrook was among the first schools to introduce the English Speaking Board exams, affectionately known as OE (Oral English). These exams have become an integral part of our school’s culture, providing children from Year 1 to Year 8 with the confidence to speak in public.
The structure of the exams has remained consistent over the years. Each child gives a talk, reads an excerpt chosen by the examiner from a book they particularly enjoyed, and recites a poem or a piece of drama they have learned. Marks are also awarded for their ability to ask and answer questions.
While the children often feel anxious during their first attempt, they usually wish they could redo it immediately afterward and always look forward to the OE exams the following year.
We maintain exceptionally high standards, with many distinctions awarded each year. Our school’s strong reputation ensures that ESB examiners are eager to return, recognising the quality of our pupils’ performances.
